newsitem.title: GERMANY: Swissair rules out ex-Germany rates hike.
newsitem.headline: Swissair rules out ex-Germany rates hike.

text.p: Swissair said it will ignore the ex-Germany air cargo rates rises of Lufthansa Cargo AG and keep its rates stable this autumn.
Ulf Steinmann, Swissair cargo manager Germany, told Reuters in an interview the airline maintained prices during a summer price war and thus did not need to regain lost rates levels.
Lufthansa Cargo said on Monday it will raise ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent to Bangkok, Singapore and Hong Kong from October 1.
Steinmann said Lufthansa started a price war with its summer incentive scheme offering agents a 2.5 percent bonus for beating agreed targets as well and with large-scale ad-hoc rates offers.
Forwarders had switched volumes from Swissair to Lufthansa to take advantage of these deals, he disclosed.
Steinmann said: "I decided not to take part in this price war. This has cost me, especially in June, July and August where I did not reach the previous year's levels.
"I find it a shame that clients followed the Lufthansa temptations and left us," he added.

"But that puts me in the comfortable situation where I do not need to give my clients price increases. We kept going in the summer and will keep our standard rates in the winter with very minor adaptations," Steinmann said.
The only rises would be on some African and east European routes, he said.
Steinmann added: "I see no signs that exports will improve in the autumn. Everyone talks about a recovery in the export market but I do not know where it will come from.
"There is simply too much capacity on the market everywhere."
